# Palette (generated by tools/palette_check.py from figures/style.py; do not edit by hand)

One palette for every figure; `figures/style.py` is the only place colours are defined, and every module of the figures/ package imports it. Preview with simulated colour-vision deficiency: [palette_preview.png](palette_preview.png).

## Rules

* **Source**: the palette is inspired by Francis Bacon, *Head VI* (1949): golds, mauves, deep blues and browns on a near-black ground. The hue families are fixed by that choice; lightness and chroma were set by maximising the minimum CAM02-UCS distance of every group below under every simulated deficiency.
* **Strategies** (palette.toml [strategies]): S1 Avoid #DFA538, S2 Switch #8D6545, S3 Improve #4A6192. A lever is drawn in its strategy colour and told apart by marker (o, s, ^, D, v within a strategy; SF10). The Moderate / Ambitious Pathway vermilion (#EB6123) and TL a deep forest green (#13412B; a larger circle on point plots).
* **Demand bands** (palette.toml [demand_bands]) keep the hue families of the former lever shades (2026 overbuild the deep mauve anchor, Overbuild absorbed a lighter mauve (#9E5B7F), Demolition replacement a lilac (#D0BBDC), Unconsented additions a darker lilac (#5C9CC5), the Recent replacement surge a pale mauve (#8A66AB) with a fine light hatch (the only hatched band), Released dwellings (TL) a light green (#95C283)). The only untargeted band, Population growth, is a solid deep green-blue (#586E71). Unexplained building of the history: a faded reddish face (#D98B5F).
* **Signs**: the data keep the sign of every band and the figures never flip it. Time series: positive bands stacked up from zero, negative bands down from zero (fixed order), the net a black line. Cumulative bars: positives stacked; each negative band an unfilled, unhatched segment outlined in its band colour, hanging from the top of the positive stack, so the bar ends at its net total, marked by a net tick; one legend entry per band. Materials and stages are never negative (a STOP if they were).
* **Maintenance** (B2, B4) neutral grey (#9E9E9E); committed emissions after 2050 a lighter grey drawn hollow (#D0D0D0). Carbon stages (palette.toml [life_cycle_stages]): A1-A3 #4A6192, A4-A5 #ABD3FA, soil carbon loss #8D6545.
* **Reference** dark grey (#4D4D4D); Low and High replacement mid greys with dashed and dotted lines. The Fig3b 2026-2050 column (palette.toml [cumulative]): #4D4D4D.
* **One at a time** (palette.toml [one_at_a_time]; Fig7a, ED4, ED5): input at its low end #4A6192, at its high end #EB6123, a single alternative case #6E6E6E.
* **Stacked bars and areas** are drawn seamless: each segment's edge is its own face colour at 0.3 pt (no white borders, no anti-aliasing gaps); a hatch is drawn in a thin hatch colour only (default #6E6E6E; the surge band #FFFFFF). Legend handles keep a thin grey outline.
* **Boundaries** (every planetary-boundary figure, one implementation in style.py; colours from palette.toml [boundaries] and [boundary_zones], the zone opacities fixed in style.ZONE_ALPHA): acquired rights (AR) thin red line (#D7191C), ability to pay (AtP) thin dark-red dotted line (#67000D); zones below AtP faded green (#41AB5D, alpha 0.3), between AtP and AR light green (#A1D99B, alpha 0.3) and above AR light red (#FB6A4A, alpha 0.07, "boundary exceeded"), on annual, cumulative and level-of-exceedance axes alike. The two principles are never averaged.
* **Settings**: lines: Moderate solid bold, Ambitious the same colour thin dotted; markers: Moderate filled, Ambitious hollow; bars (Fig7): Moderate hollow, Ambitious filled, TL a large deep-green dot.
* **Typeface**: Liberation Sans only (metric-compatible with Arial), bundled in `fonts/` under the SIL Open Font License 1.1, registered by figures/style.py, so every machine renders the same glyphs.
* **Sizes** (Nature Cities): width 89 mm (single column) or 183 mm (double column), page depth at most 247 mm; text 7 pt, legends and ticks 6 pt, never below 5 pt; data lines 1 pt, emphasised lines 1.5 pt, grid and edges 0.5 pt.
* **Files** (run profiles, runprofile.py): light PNG at 200 dpi with a small grey footer "LIGHT RUN — n=1000"; full PDF (TrueType fonts embedded) + PNG at 600 dpi; no software or date metadata, so re-runs are byte-identical.
* **Materials** (Fig3b and the diagnostics): the six stripes of the Pride flag in one order in every figure (author decision), soil carbon loss faded on top (no hatch); kept because the material figures label every layer directly (see the check below).

## Colour-vision-deficiency check

Minimum pairwise distance within each group (CAM02-UCS, Luo, Cui & Li 2006) after simulating the deficiency at full severity (Machado, Oliveira & Fernandes 2009; colorspacious 1.1.2). Threshold for "clearly distinguishable" adjacent fills: 10 (stated convention).

Groups below the threshold: Boundary zones on white (every boundary figure); Demand bands (Fig1, Fig2, Fig5, ED6, D25, D26, D36); Projection variants and boundaries (ED2, ED9); History bands (Fig1); Fig3 (runs, boundaries, zones on white, cumulative column). Why each still reads: the boundary zones are pale by design (data drawn over them), always bounded by the AR and AtP lines and ordered strictly in lightness (darker green < light green < palest red under every simulated deficiency), so their order survives without hue; any other group below the threshold is labelled directly in every figure (text on or beside each layer) or carries a hatch, so the reading never depends on colour alone.

Historical replacement against the Recent replacement surge face: normal 30.4, deuteranomaly 30.9, protanomaly 31.3, tritanomaly 28.9 (below the threshold by design: told apart by lightness, a slightly different hue and the surge's fine light hatch, and labelled in every figure).

## Boundary zones: lightness order

J' of each zone on white (normal, deuteranomaly, protanomaly, tritanomaly): Within both budgets (below AtP) 89.6 / 89.6 / 90.9 / 89.4; Within AR only (between AtP and AR) 95.1 / 95.2 / 95.8 / 95.0; Boundary exceeded (above AR) 97.8 / 97.9 / 97.4 / 97.6. Strictly increasing under every vision type: yes. redraw.py warns when a palette breaks this order.

## Sequential ramp

Continuous fields (the solution space, Fig6) use one blue ramp, light to dark; its CAM02-UCS lightness J' must fall strictly so the order survives greyscale: `#EAF2FB` 96, `#C6DBF2` 88, `#9EC5F4` 80, `#6DA7EC` 69, `#3987E5` 57, `#256ABF` 46, `#184F95` 35, `#0D366B` 24 (monotone).

## Sources

* Luo MR, Cui G, Li C (2006) Uniform colour spaces based on CIECAM02 colour appearance model. Color Research & Application 31, 320-330.
* Machado GM, Oliveira MM, Fernandes LAF (2009) A physiologically-based model for simulation of color vision deficiency. IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics 15, 1291-1298.
* Okabe M, Ito K (2008) Color Universal Design (CUD): how to make figures and presentations that are friendly to colorblind people. https://jfly.uni-koeln.de/color/ (the categorical palette).
* Smith NJ, van der Walt S, colorspacious 1.1.2 (Python package), https://github.com/njsmith/colorspacious.
